proposals.before: In his youth Chongwei entered the service of Emperor Mingzong, advancing from a guardsman in the Imperial Guard to prefect of Fangzhou.
proposals.after: In his youth Chongwei entered the service of Emperor Mingzong, advancing from a guardsman in the Imperial Guard to acting prefect of Fangzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 領防州刺史 marks acting or concurrent tenure, which the literal already has and the idiomatic omits.

proposals.before: Before long he was reassigned to Yanzhou and promoted to commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry.
proposals.after: Before long he was reassigned to Yunzhou and promoted to commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou would be 兗州.

proposals.before: Before long he was transferred to govern at Yan Prefecture and promoted to commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces.
proposals.after: Before long he was transferred to govern at Yun Prefecture and promoted to commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture.

proposals.before: In the second year he led a great army south against Xin Prefecture, Mancheng, and Suicheng.
proposals.after: In the second year he led a great army and took Xin Prefecture, Mancheng, and Suicheng.
proposals.reason: 下 here means that the army took the towns, not that it marched south against them.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu's court reached the capital, Chongwei was appointed military governor of Songzhou and acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu's court reached the capital, Chongwei was appointed military governor of Songzhou and acting Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 守太尉 is the Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu's imperial carriage reached the capital, Chongwei was made military governor of Song Prefecture and additionally acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu's imperial carriage reached the capital, Chongwei was made military governor of Song Prefecture and additionally acting Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 加守太尉 names the office Taiwei, not Taishi.

proposals.before: In the spring of the first Kaiyun year the enemy struck Chan and Wei, and the Young Emperor went to Chanzhou in person. The Khitan general Maduo crossed at Majiakou in Yanzhou with a flanking force and fortified the east bank. Shouzhen raced from Chanzhou to meet him.
proposals.after: In the spring of the first Kaiyun year the enemy struck Chan and Wei, and the Young Emperor went to Chanzhou in person. The Khitan general Maduo crossed at Majiakou in Yunzhou with a flanking force and fortified the east bank. Shouzhen raced from Chanzhou to meet him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州). The crossing at 馬家口 is therefore in Yunzhou.

proposals.before: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun the enemy masses invaded Chan and Wei; the Young Emperor went in person to Chan Prefecture. The Khitan sent the general Maduo with a surprise force to cross the river at Majiakou in Yan Prefecture and erect palisades on the east bank. Shouzhen led troops in a rush from Chan Prefecture to meet them.
proposals.after: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun the enemy masses invaded Chan and Wei; the Young Emperor went in person to Chan Prefecture. The Khitan sent the general Maduo with a surprise force to cross the river at Majiakou in Yun Prefecture and erect palisades on the east bank. Shouzhen led troops in a rush from Chan Prefecture to meet them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 should be rendered Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture.

proposals.before: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace guard and was posted to Yanzhou, nursing considerable resentment.
proposals.after: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace guard and was posted to Yunzhou, nursing considerable resentment.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou would be 兗州, already used earlier in the chapter for a different posting.

proposals.before: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces and was transferred to govern Yan Prefecture, his mind rather resentful and dissatisfied.
proposals.after: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces and was transferred to govern Yun Prefecture, his mind rather resentful and dissatisfied.
proposals.reason: 移鎮鄆州 is a transfer to Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture.

proposals.before: Soon enemy cavalry crossed secretly to Luancheng and severed the supply lines. Wang Qing was killed in battle, and Du Chongwei surrendered with Shouzhen to the Khitan. Shouzhen was made Minister of Education and kept Yanzhou, then followed the Khitan to Bian.
proposals.after: Soon enemy cavalry crossed secretly to Luancheng and severed the supply lines. Wang Qing was killed in battle, and Du Chongwei surrendered with Shouzhen to the Khitan. Shouzhen was made Minister of Education and kept Yunzhou, then followed the Khitan to Bian.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州); the idiomatic rendering conflates the two prefectures.

proposals.before: Before long enemy horsemen secretly crossed to Luancheng and cut our supply routes; soon Wang Qing died in battle, and Du Chongwei then surrendered with Shouzhen to the Khitan. Shouzhen was appointed Minister of Education and remained military governor of Yan Prefecture as before, following the Khitan to Bian.
proposals.after: Before long enemy horsemen secretly crossed to Luancheng and cut our supply routes; soon Wang Qing died in battle, and Du Chongwei then surrendered with Shouzhen to the Khitan. Shouzhen was appointed Minister of Education and remained military governor of Yun Prefecture as before, following the Khitan to Bian.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 鄆州 as Yan Prefecture; the source prefecture is Yun.

proposals.before: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu Hou had first been married to Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun, military governor of Hezhong.
proposals.after: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu Hou had first been married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen, the military governor of Hezhong.
proposals.reason: The phrase 河中節度使 modifies 李守貞, not 崇訓; the literal English wrongly makes Chongxun the Hezhong governor.

proposals.before: Shouzhen believed it and therefore said, "If my wife is yet to be empress, what may be known of me?"
proposals.after: Shouzhen believed it and therefore said, "If my daughter-in-law is yet to be empress, what may be known of me?"
proposals.reason: In this supplement 吾婦 refers to Fu Hou, already identified as the wife of Shouzhen's son, not as Shouzhen's own wife.

proposals.before: He soon sent envoys to submit to Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, who replied with a forged edict making him military governor of Jinchang and acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He soon sent envoys to submit to Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, who replied with a forged edict making him military governor of Jinchang and acting Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is acting Taiwei (Grand Commandant), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: Before long he sent men with submission to Hezhong; Li Shouzhen sent envoys bearing a false edict appointing Siwan military governor of the Jinchang army and acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: Before long he sent men with submission to Hezhong; Li Shouzhen sent envoys bearing a false edict appointing Siwan military governor of the Jinchang army and acting Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is acting Taiwei (Grand Commandant), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: In the summer of the second year, with food exhausted and no way out, retired general Li Su, living in the city, spoke with aide Cheng Rangneng to Siwan: "Your Excellency had no quarrel with the throne. You rebelled only from fear of execution.
proposals.after: In the summer of the second year, with food exhausted and no way out, retired Left Brave Guards senior general Li Su, living in the city, spoke with aide Cheng Rangneng to Siwan: "Your Excellency had no quarrel with the throne. You rebelled only from fear of execution.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 左驍衛上將軍, leaving only 'retired general' and omitting the specific office in the Chinese.

proposals.before: The court is fighting on three fronts and has not yet taken one rebel city. If you turn back now and surrender first, your service may yet redeem your fault.
proposals.after: The court is fighting on three fronts and has not yet taken one city. If you turn back now and surrender first, your service may yet redeem your fault.
proposals.reason: 一城未下 is 'one city not yet taken'; the idiomatic insertion of 'rebel' is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Thereafter the lady secretly had Siwan's wife visit court, lavished clothing on her, and gave her large sums of money and goods over time.
proposals.after: Thereafter the lady secretly had Siwan's wife come to pay respects, lavished clothing on her, and gave her large sums of money and goods over time.
proposals.reason: 來參 is a visit to pay respects, not attendance at court; 'visit court' invents a setting.

proposals.before: An edict appointed him acting prefect of Huazhou and acting Grand Guardian, made Chang Yanqing prefect of Guozhou, and sent a palace official with commissions and imperial credentials.
proposals.after: An edict appointed him acting military governor of Huazhou and acting Grand Guardian, made Chang Yanqing prefect of Guozhou, and sent a palace official with commissions and imperial credentials.
proposals.reason: 華州留後 is the retainee/acting military-governor post, not 'acting prefect'; 刺史 is the prefect title used only for Chang Yanqing.

decisions.reason: 領防州刺史 marks concurrent or acting tenure of Fangzhou. The idiomatic field drops 領 and leaves only a full prefecture, while the proposed wording restores that distinction without other changes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自護聖軍校領防州刺史

decisions.reason: 移鎮鄆州 names Yunzhou. Yanzhou would be 兗州; the original English conflates the two prefectures.
The same 鄆州 is Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture. The literal replacement corrects the place name and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
領大軍下新州、滿城、遂城 uses 下 for capturing the towns. 'South against' invents a direction and misses the taking.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 領大軍下新州、滿城、遂城

decisions.reason: 加守太尉 is the Grand Commandant (太尉). Grand Preceptor would be 太師; the proposed title is the one named in the Chinese.
The literal field likewise renders 太尉 as Grand Preceptor. Replacing it with Grand Commandant matches 守太尉.
由鄆州馬家口濟河 places the crossing at Majiakou in Yunzhou. Yanzhou would be 兗州, a different prefecture.
The literal English makes the same error, rendering 鄆州 as Yan Prefecture. Yun Prefecture is the correct name.
移鎮鄆州 is a posting to Yunzhou. The original Yanzhou would correspond to 兗州, already a distinct place in this chapter.
The literal transfer is likewise to Yun Prefecture, not Yan Prefecture. The rest of the sentence is already accurate.
依前鄆州節度使 keeps Shouzhen as military governor of Yunzhou. Rendering that post as Yanzhou conflates 鄆州 with 兗州.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 鄆州 as Yan Prefecture. Yun Prefecture is required by the Chinese.
河中節度使李守貞之子崇訓 makes Li Shouzhen, not Chongxun, the Hezhong governor. The original apposition wrongly assigns that office to the son.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 河中節度使李守貞之子崇訓

decisions.reason: In this supplement 吾婦 refers to Fu Hou, already identified as Chongxun's wife and thus Shouzhen's daughter-in-law, not Shouzhen's own wife.
檢校太尉 is a nominal Grand Commandant. Grand Preceptor would be 太師; the proposed office matches the Chinese title.
The literal field has the same 太尉/太師 confusion. Acting Grand Commandant is the correct rendering of 檢校太尉.
左驍衛上將軍致仕 names Li Su's specific retired office. 'Retired general' omits that title, which the proposed wording restores.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 左驍衛上將軍致仕李肅

decisions.reason: 一城未下 says one city has not yet fallen. Inserting 'rebel' adds a qualifier absent from the speech; removing it restores the Chinese.
來參 is a visit to pay respects to the lady, not attendance at court. 'Visit court' invents an imperial setting the Chinese does not name.
華州留後 is the retainee or acting military-governor post. Prefect would be 刺史, the title given only to Chang Yanqing as 虢州刺史.

claimRevisions.reason: The claim's Chinese place is 鄆州, but the English value follows the mistranslation Yanzhou. The accepted repair shows the posting is to Yunzhou.
